title: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not: A Functional Comparison of the Platonic and Aristotelian Corpora, and the Insufficiency of Lexical Measurement for Maker-Count (EA-MEASURES-REPORT-01)
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: The technical report behind the measured section of a companion article under review, whose title is withheld here so that this deposit is not a prior circulation of it. Part I reports the investigation's one positive measurement: a six-function specification of a transmission apparatus — encoding, substrate, decommissioning, withholding, recovery, verification — generated in a separate investigation of textual transmission, registered before any Platonic or Aristotelian text was assigned to it, and filled by both corpora at the level of the individual work, with one device closely transformed across the boundary and no cross-reference; with its four rival specifications, its random control on the Johannine writings (0/6 by what a work is about, 6/6 by what appears in it), and the concession that keeps it from being more than it is. Part II reports the instruments that read lexical distribution — fifteen features, every one destroyed by a control run in the same session (corpus size; Greek word order; period and dialect; coverage geometry collapsing from 66.8 to 18.8 under size-matching); the object-conditioning result (0.1033 above every synthetic five-author pool, falling within domain to 0.0571 against Plato's 0.0570, with the parity's base rate stated as unrun); the validation check (one of three; Plato|Xenophon classed SAME); the school rival measured three ways with limits (the naming-gap reflex at 0.00 in 1,140,474 tokens of Albert against 2.60/8.43 in the Greek pair; the school default; the naming asymmetry); and the formal result the title states. What the instruments return on maker-count is a null in either direction, symmetric between one maker and master-and-pupil; the report makes no argument about authorship and does not depend on the article for any number.

wiki_article: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not (EA-MEASURES-REPORT-01) is the technical report standing behind the measured section of a companion article on the relation between the Platonic and Aristotelian corpora, deposited under its own title so that the article remains uncirculated while under review. Part I reports the investigation's one positive measurement: a six-function specification of a transmission apparatus — encoding, substrate, decommissioning, withholding, recovery, verification — generated in a separate investigation and registered before any Platonic or Aristotelian text was assigned to it, which both corpora fill at the level of the individual work, with four rival specifications and a random control that fills nothing when works are assigned by what they are about and everything when assigned by what appears in them. Part II reports the instruments that read lexical distribution and the control that destroyed each of them: corpus size, Greek word order, period and dialect, coverage geometry collapsing under size-matching, and a validation check that classified two known-different authors as one. What the instruments return on the count of makers is a null in either direction, and the null is symmetric — the same instruments that say nothing about one maker say nothing about master and pupil, so the partition they helped build they cannot certify. The report makes no argument about authorship; it records what was measured, under what conditions, and what each result cannot support, with the base rates that remain unrun named so that they can be run against it. Its sources are the notebook and the measurement register deposited alongside it.

entities.subject: transmission apparatus (six-function specification)
entities.object: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not: A Functional Comparison of the Platonic and Aristoteli
entities.note: A six-function specification — encoding (T1), substrate (T2), decommissioning (T3), withholding (T4), recovery (T5), verification (T6) — generated externally and registered before any Platonic or Aristotelian text was assigned, used as a test apparatus rather than a description.

entities.subject: sharpness (slot-fill metric)
entities.object: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not: A Functional Comparison of the Platonic and Aristoteli
entities.note: A measure of how distinctly a corpus fills the slots of the transmission apparatus, defined as the ratio of slots filled by distinct works; Plato scores 1.00 (six slots, six dialogues) and Aristotle 0.83 (six slots, five works with one doubling).

entities.subject: received-characterisation assignment rule
entities.object: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not: A Functional Comparison of the Platonic and Aristoteli
entities.note: The rule that apparatus slots are assigned only from received characterisation of what each work is about — not from what appears in it — making the measure a test rather than a description; validated by the Johannine control.

entities.subject: object-conditioning (dispersion)
entities.object: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not: A Functional Comparison of the Platonic and Aristoteli
entities.note: The phenomenon by which Aristotle's high internal dispersion is almost entirely explained by variation in subject domain rather than by multiple authorship; when domain is held constant, within-domain dispersion becomes numerically indistinguishable from Plato's overall dispersion.

entities.subject: object-space (of a domain)
entities.object: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not: A Functional Comparison of the Platonic and Aristoteli
entities.note: A characterisation of the heterogeneity of subject matter within a domain, used to explain the ordering of within-domain dispersions across Aristotle's domains; described by the range and internal variety of objects a domain treats.

entities.subject: naming-gap reflex
entities.object: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not: A Functional Comparison of the Platonic and Aristoteli
entities.note: The pattern of halting at an unnamed class, flagging it (ἀνώνυμον, Latin innominat-), and coining a term; measured per 100k tokens against a division-density denominator, shared by the Platonic and Aristotelian corpora and not transmitted to the documented scholastic master-student pair.

entities.subject: αὐτεπιτακτική
entities.object: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not: A Functional Comparison of the Platonic and Aristoteli
entities.note: A coinage from the Platonic Statesman for the art that issues commands from itself rather than relaying another's mind; contrasted with ἑρμηνεία and identified as a naming-gap instance in the corpus.

entities.subject: σύμβολον (as analytic concept)
entities.object: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not: A Functional Comparison of the Platonic and Aristoteli
entities.note: Used technically to characterise the conjunction of maximal substrate separation and maximal functional interlock: halves that do not resemble each other and only fit, as the deposit defines it in its comparison sample.

entities.subject: heteronymic architecture (typology)
entities.object: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not: A Functional Comparison of the Platonic and Aristoteli
entities.note: A typological distinction between heteronymic systems that close by progressive subtraction toward a remainder (Pessoa's model) and those that close by complementary coverage of positions; the deposit argues these are distinct types with different evidential implications.

entities.subject: coverage geometry
entities.object: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not: A Functional Comparison of the Platonic and Aristoteli
entities.note: A distributional measure assessing what proportion of a master corpus's ground is covered by a student corpus, using contiguous fixed-size windows; shown to collapse under size-matching and to read corpus size rather than relation-type.

entities.subject: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not (formal result)
entities.object: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not: A Functional Comparison of the Platonic and Aristoteli
entities.note: The deposit's formal conclusion: that master-student inheritance between authorial positions is detectable by distributional instruments, but how many embodied makers occupied those positions is not thereby detectable.

entities.subject: completion-across-the-boundary
entities.object: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not: A Functional Comparison of the Platonic and Aristoteli
entities.note: The specific finding that T2 (substrate slot) is not merely matched between corpora but completed: the Theaetetus opens a route and declares it impossible, and De anima 424a retains the machinery and supplies the missing element (ἄνευ τῆς ὕλης) without cross-reference.

entities.subject: errores coniunctivi (applied to functional holes)
entities.object: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not: A Functional Comparison of the Platonic and Aristoteli
entities.note: The deposit adapts Maas's concept of shared conjunctive errors — structures that could not have been transmitted as doctrine — to apply to abandoned executions marked refuted, arguing that completing such a hole requires reading a failure as unfinished against the doctrine's own verdict.

entities.subject: remainder test (unrun)
entities.object: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not: A Functional Comparison of the Platonic and Aristoteli
entities.note: A named-but-unrun measure that would test whether anything is invariant across the two corpora's positions that is not explained by shared language, genre or subject — the measure on which the Greek pair would be the same kind of object as a documented heteronymic system.

entities.subject: school default (commentary shape)
entities.object: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not: A Functional Comparison of the Platonic and Aristoteli
entities.note: The characterisation that a school of transmission defaults to commentary, which has an opposite shape to unannounced transformative interlock: a documented pupil cites and expands his master rather than completing abandoned figures silently.

entities.subject: dispersion parity (0.0571 / 0.0570)
entities.object: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not: A Functional Comparison of the Platonic and Aristoteli
entities.note: The finding that Aristotle's within-domain dispersion (0.0571), after object-conditioning, is numerically indistinguishable from Plato's total dispersion (0.0570), with a gap of one ten-thousandth occurring zero times in 55 pairs of the seated corpora.

entities.subject: mimesis in the Republic III sense (moved from voice to form)
entities.object: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not: A Functional Comparison of the Platonic and Aristoteli
entities.note: A reading in which Aristotle's lack of consistent style across domains is interpreted as the treatise-form analogue of the tragedian disappearing into character — the treatise disappears into its object — derived from Republic III's account of mimetic narration.

entities.subject: ἐντελεχείᾳ μὲν μία, δυνάμει δὲ πλείονες (corpus-scale measurement)
entities.object: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not: A Functional Comparison of the Platonic and Aristoteli
entities.note: The formula from De anima II.2 (413b) — one in actuality, many in potentiality — applied at corpus scale as the measured middle term: the corpus is one when the object is held (0.0571 vs 0.0570) and many when divided by object (ratio 1.489, Z = +4.54).

entities.subject: void condition (Johannine control)
entities.object: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not: A Functional Comparison of the Platonic and Aristoteli
entities.note: The result of applying the appearance-reading rule to the Johannine group, which produced 6/6 slot-fills on content that appears in those texts but is not what any book is about, demonstrating that the received-characterisation rule is constitutive of the measure.

entities.subject: source-naming asymmetry (Aristotle/scholastics)
entities.object: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not: A Functional Comparison of the Platonic and Aristoteli
entities.note: The measured finding that Aristotle names Plato at 0.70 per 10k while Aquinas names Aristotle at 12.0–14.8 and Albert at 16.2, i.e. 17–23 times more often at comparable institutional proximity; carried as a source-naming fact with an uncontrolled Greek/Latin convention caveat.
